decision_rationale: Four of five agents recommend Pause; one (Risk/Critic) recommends Roll Back. The 10-day data shows a clear pattern: a significant degradation on Days 5-6, followed by partial recovery after the Day 7 hotfix. By Day 10, crash rate (0.95%) and latency (290ms) are trending toward thresholds but have not yet consistently met them. Three of nine metrics still breach success criteria. The critical draft-loss bug (KI-001) remains open and poses unacceptable data-integrity risk. Feature funnel completion (28.5%) and funnel completion (28.5%) are strong positive signals that argue against a full rollback. Pausing at 25% limits the blast radius to ~130,000 users while preserving the ability to resume quickly. The pause is conditional on shipping the KI-001 fix and opt-out toggle before any further expansion.

individual_verdicts.rationale: Day 10 signup conversion (3.8%) has recovered to the threshold (3.8%), but D1 retention at 68.0% barely meets the 68.0% criterion. D7 retention at 39.2% is below the 42.0% target — a concerning signal for long-term value. Feature funnel completion at 28.5% is strong and exceeds the 20.0% target. The missing opt-out toggle (KI-004) is a significant friction source. Recommend pausing at 25% until the opt-out ships and D7 retention stabilises.
key_evidence: Signup conversion Day 10: 3.8% (threshold: 3.8%)
D7 retention: 39.2% — below 42.0% target
Feature funnel completion: 28.5% — strong signal
Total cancellations over 10 days: 335 (34/day vs 10/day baseline)
recommended_actions: Freeze rollout at 25% — do not expand to the 50% cohort.
Expedite the opt-out toggle (KI-004) before any further expansion.
Run a D7 retention deep-dive to separate performance-driven churn from feature-driven churn.

P95 latency peaked at 485ms (Day 6), now 290ms — within the 300ms target. Payment success rate dipped to 97.8% on Day 6 (threshold: 99.0%). Now at 99.2%. Support tickets peaked at 289/day (Day 6) vs 38/day baseline. Now 155/day — still elevated. D7 retention (39.2%) is 5.8pp below baseline (45.0%) — statistically significant. Trends are recovering but 3 of 9 metrics still breach thresholds.

individual_verdicts.rationale: Of 35 feedback entries: 10 positive, 18 negative, 7 neutral. Negative feedback is concentrated on Days 4-6 (the trouble window) and clusters around 3 recurring themes: (1) performance/lag — 6 mentions, (2) no opt-out — 5 mentions, (3) draft data loss — 3 mentions. Two high-impact outliers: a user with a disability praising the feature (#35) and a sales email auto-complete incident that could have cost a deal (#34). App store ratings are polarised (1-star and 5-star). Reddit thread about draft data loss (PSA post) has amplification risk. Sentiment is skewed negative in the Days 4-6 window. Post-hotfix sentiment (Days 8-10) is more positive, but the missing opt-out toggle is a persistent irritant across all channels.

recommended_actions: Issue transparent status update: acknowledge performance issues, draft-loss bug, and opt-out gap.
Respond personally to the Twitter auto-complete complaints with empathy and DM follow-up.
Prepare accessibility-focused case study with user #35's permission — powerful positive narrative.
Do NOT run any promotional campaigns for Smart Compose until opt-out toggle ships.
Monitor Reddit thread on draft loss — if it trends, issue an official response.

individual_verdicts.rationale: KI-001 (draft data loss) remains in 'investigating' status after 10 days — this is a critical severity bug that has been reported by 3 separate users and amplified on Reddit. At 25% rollout (130,000 users exposed), the blast radius for a data-loss bug is unacceptable. Cancellations averaged 34/day over 10 days vs 10/day baseline — a 3.4x increase that would scale further at full rollout. D7 retention at 39.2% is below the 42.0% threshold — the feature may be driving users away. The Day 7 hotfix improved latency but crash rate (0.95%) still exceeds the 0.75% threshold. Extrapolating to 50% rollout carries infrastructure risk given KI-002's partial fix status. The team may be anchored on the recovery trend rather than the absolute breach of success criteria.

recommended_actions: Roll back to pre-launch state for the 25% cohort — data-loss risk is too high.
If rollback is rejected: freeze at 25%, mandate KI-001 fix within 48h, add opt-out toggle.
Commission independent review of the inference API scaling before any expansion.
Conduct blameless post-incident review covering the Day 5-6 degradation.
individual_verdicts.dissent_notes: The majority leans toward Pause, but pausing at 25% still exposes ~130k users to a data-loss bug (KI-001) with no confirmed fix. The recovery trend is only 3 days old (Day 7 hotfix) and has not been stress-tested at higher rollout. The draft-disappearing bug alone warrants rollback — it is a trust-destroying event and 3 users have already reported it. If even 0.1% of the 130k cohort experiences data loss, that's 130 affected users with high churn and social amplification risk.

individual_verdicts.rationale: The Day 7 hotfix materially improved performance: latency dropped from 485ms → 290ms (1.5x baseline, within the 300ms target). Crash rate improved from 2.4% → 0.95% but still exceeds the 0.75% threshold. KI-001 (draft loss race condition) is the highest-priority item — root cause is identified (auto-save debounce vs suggestion overlay teardown) and a fix is feasible in 24-48h. KI-002 (latency scaling) hotfix is deployed; further tuning requires load testing at 50% traffic before expansion. KI-004 (opt-out toggle) is ~4 engineering days from ship. Full rollback is costly (~6 engineer-hours + deployment risk + user confusion) and would lose the 28.5% adoption signal. A pause + targeted fixes is the better path.
